Morgan Stanley
Interview Experience - Harsh Nag (TY B.Tech- CS)
Round 1 : Online coding round on 27th July, 2022
●Section 1 : Coding Section
1) This was a question related to greedy. I was able to solve this
question, passing half of the total test cases.
2) Given the binary tree the task was to output the boundary
traversal of the tree. The question was overall easy as it was a
standard question of binary trees. I was able to solve this
question and passed all the test cases.
Reference link : Boundary traversal
3) This was just the standard one given in complicated language.
The question was of Counting Inversions into the array. I was
able to pass partial test cases due to a slight error in my code
which I wasn't able to debug due to time limitations.
Reference Link : Counting Inversion
●Section 2 :  Debugging section
This section was quite easy. I was able to solve 6 correctly out of
7. The questions are basically related to syntax or logical errors.
One can easily pass this section if one has a habit of debugging
the code on their own.
●Section 3 : Aptitude section
This section was also easy, I was able to solve 5-6 questions on
my own and the rest of the questions, I marked randomly due to
time constraint 🤡 and also there was no negative marking.
The questions were based on probability, permutation &
combination and mathematical calculations.

(After this round only 17 were shortlisted for the offline interview
round.)
Round 2 : Technical Round ( 1st August, 2022 at 9:30 AM. Lasted for
1 Hr 20 mins )
●Firstly, I was asked to introduce myself (prepare a good
introduction of yourself prior to the interview as it is one of the
obvious questions.)
●Then as soon as I was done introducing myself the interviewer
asked me about my projects which were there in my resume. I
gave a detailed explanation of my projects like what was the aim
of making a project and how it actually worked. He also asked
me about the challenges which I faced while making these
projects. (Go through the projects you make once before the
interviews )
●Then the interviewer asked me to rate myself in terms of coding.
So I told him 8 out of 10.
●Then he started asking me DSA questions 🙂:
1) Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return
total number of subarrays whose sum is equal to k.
Sample Input 1: nums=[1,1,1], k=2
Sample Output 1 : 2
Explanation : There are 2 subarrays - one from index 0 to
index 1 ({1,1}) and another from index 1 to index 2 ({1,1})
whose sum is 2.
Sample Input 2 : nums=[1,2,3], k=3
Sample Output 2 : 2
Explanation : There are 2 subarrays -  one from index 0 to
index 1({1,2}) and another is just index 2 ({3}).
So I started giving the Brute Force solution - Find all the
subarrays using two nested for loops and then calculate
the sum for each subarray. The subarray whose sum is
equal to k will be included in the final answer.
He asked me about the time and space complexity of the
solution so it was O(n^2) in terms of time and O(1) in terms
of space.

nums[0] < k && nums[0]>answer, so answer=nums[0]
So answer=2
For i=1;
nums[1] < k && nums[1]>answer, so answer=nums[1]
So answer=5
For i=2;
nums[2] !< k , so no change
For i=3;
nums[3]  !< k, so no change
For i=4
nums[4] < k && nums[4] >answer, so answer=nums[4]
So answer=6
Which is correct.
The  time complexity of this solution was O(n)
But then he told me to optimize this approach.
Then I was a bit confused about how to further reduce the
complexity. So then I thought of an algorithm like binary
search because the time complexity less than O(n) is O(log
n).
But to apply something like binary search, we need an
array in a sorted manner. So I told the interviewer that the
algo can be something like binary search but we need to
first sort the array. But in that case the complexity will
increase to O(n log n). Then he told me that he never
mentioned the group of integers in the array. Then the first
thing that came to my mind was SET. We will take the
input in SET which will keep the integers in the sorted
manner and then we can apply algorithms like binary
search.But then too we need to insert the element into the
set which will be taking O(n log n) time complexity. But
then he mentioned that the time complexity of the input
will not be considered. So then  the task was simple.
Take the Integers into SET whose time complexity will not
be considered and then just apply the algo like binary
search and then the complexity will be O(log n).
Interviewer didn’t ask me how I would implement that
Binary search algo. What he asked me is the difference
between a hash set and a tree set. This was the only

question I wasn't able to answer🤢. I told him that I know
only one difference: that hash set can store multiple copies
of the same element and tree set cannot. How they
internally worked that I couldn’t recollect. So he moved on
to the next part.
●He then started asking me about core CS fundamentals.
●He asked me about:
1) Paging
2) Segmentation
3) Internal and External Fragmentation
4) Contiguous and non-contiguous memory allocation
( All these questions were the standard ones and I explained
everything in detail. Interviewer was satisfied with my answers )
●Then he asked me about Object Oriented Programming
concepts.
1) He asked me to design the online transaction system
(System Design) which I designed using the concepts of
OOPS like inheritance, abstraction and encapsulation.
2) Then he asked me about the abstract classes and interface
and the differences between them.
(He was satisfied with my answers.)
After this round 11 were shortlisted for the HR round.
Round 3 : HR Round ( 1st August,2022 at 3:30 AM. Lasted for 45
mins )
●This round was very casual for me because the interviewer and I
shared many similar thoughts.
●He asked me about my interests, my family and gave me some
situations and asked me about how I will react to those
situations. He was very satisfied with my point of view and
thoughts.
●Then he asked me whether I have some questions regarding the
company (Always ask something- this shows that you are
interested in the company). I had already prepared some
standard questions to ask them prior to the interview 😈🤡 .
On 8th August, 2022, 8 candidates were offered internship and I was

lucky to be one of them.
